name: SMART Recovery (Self-Management and Recovery Training)
description: Science-based alternative to 12-step programs. Provides support for people with addictions using cognitive behavioral approaches.

sections.title: About SMART Recovery
sections.text: SMART Recovery (Self-Management and Recovery Training) is a global community of mutual-support groups that help people recover from all types of addiction and addictive behaviors. Unlike 12-step programs, SMART Recovery is a science-based approach grounded in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and rational emotive behavior therapy (REBT). The program teaches practical skills for building motivation, coping with urges, managing thoughts and behaviors, and living a balanced life. SMART Recovery is secular and does not require belief in a higher power.

sections.title: The Four-Point Program
sections.text: SMART Recovery's approach centers on four key points: Building and maintaining motivation to change; Coping with urges to use; Managing thoughts, feelings, and behaviors; and Living a balanced life. Each point includes specific tools and techniques that participants learn and practice. The program emphasizes self-empowerment and developing internal resources rather than relying on external support indefinitely. Participants learn to identify and dispute irrational beliefs that contribute to addictive behavior and replace them with healthier thinking patterns.

sections.title: Types of Meetings and Support
sections.text: SMART Recovery offers multiple ways to participate: in-person meetings held at community locations nationwide and worldwide, online meetings via video conference, and 24/7 online message board communities. Meetings are typically 90 minutes and are led by trained volunteer facilitators. Unlike some programs, SMART Recovery welcomes cross-talk and discussion during meetings. Specialized meetings are available for specific populations including family and friends of those with addiction, teens, and people in the criminal justice system.

sections.title: Getting Started with SMART Recovery
sections.text: Anyone struggling with addiction can attend SMART Recovery meetings free of charge. Visit smartrecovery.org to find meetings near you or join an online meeting from anywhere. The website offers free resources including the SMART Recovery Handbook, toolbox exercises, and educational videos. New participants are encouraged to attend several meetings to learn the program's tools and techniques. Unlike some recovery programs, SMART does not require lifelong attendance—members are encouraged to graduate when they feel ready to manage their recovery independently.

sections.title: SMART Recovery Family & Friends
sections.text: SMART Recovery offers a dedicated program for family members and friends affected by a loved one's addiction. The Family & Friends program teaches the CRAFT (Community Reinforcement and Family Training) approach, an evidence-based method that helps families improve communication, set boundaries, encourage treatment-seeking, and take care of their own well-being. Family meetings provide support and practical skills, regardless of whether the person with addiction is in recovery. Like the main program, Family & Friends is free, confidential, and available both in-person and online.
